note.note:
History:
- Chief complaint: New-onset severe headache for ~1 day.
- Onset/Duration: Began on waking yesterday morning; persistent with fluctuating intensity.
- Character/Location: Left-sided, throbbing; baseline present with intermittent worsening.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia. No visual changes, no abnormal smells/tastes, no nausea/vomiting, no weakness/tingling/numbness, no skin changes/rash, no URI symptoms. Has not checked temperature; does not feel feverish.
- Triggers/Modifying factors: Worsens with bright light/sunlight; feels better lying down. No worsening with bending forward, coughing, or sneezing. Eating and drinking okay.
- Prior history of headaches: None. First episode of this kind.
- Menstrual history: Last period ~1 week ago; no clear cycle association reported.
- Family history: Mother with hypertension and migraines.
- Social: Lives with housemates. Alcohol: a few drinks on weekends. No smoking. No illicit drugs.
- Context: Possible work-related stress noted by patient.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: None reported.
- Surgeries/Hospitalizations: None reported.
- Allergies: Aspirin — causes nausea (patient-reported).
- Medications:
  - Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive); dose/route/frequency not documented; started ~6 years ago; no significant side effects reported.
  - Paracetamol (acetaminophen) taken for current headache; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Has taken NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen/naproxen) in the past; none in last few days.

Physical Examination:
- Conducted via remote consult; no vitals obtained.
- Patient-reported findings:
  - Photophobia present.
  - No visual disturbance.
  - No focal neurologic symptoms (no weakness, tingling, numbness).
  - No rash or other skin changes.
  - No runny nose, ear pain, or other URI symptoms.
  - No vomiting; maintaining oral intake.
  - No positional worsening reported; lying down provides some relief.
  - Temperature not checked at home; does not feel feverish.

Impression:
- New-onset unilateral throbbing headache with photophobia, consistent with probable migraine without aura; no red-flag features elicited on history.

Management Plan:
- Analgesia: Trial an NSAID (e.g., ibuprofen) together with paracetamol/acetaminophen; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Hydration: Increase oral fluids.
- Monitoring/Safety-net:
  - Seek medical attention urgently if headache worsens, changes character, persists without improvement, fever develops, or rash appears.
  - Contact clinic if recurrent headaches occur, if a menstrual pattern emerges, or if identifiable triggers develop.
- Preventive/Other:
  - Arrange to have blood pressure checked (has not been checked in ~6 months).
  - Obtain a home thermometer to monitor for fever.

Patient Summary:
- Patient with first episode of a left-sided, throbbing headache with photophobia for one day and no neurologic or systemic red flags. Clinical picture suggests probable migraine without aura.
- Plan is symptomatic management with NSAID plus paracetamol, hydration, and close monitoring, with instructions on when to seek urgent care and to check BP.

Key Takeaways:
- Take ibuprofen with paracetamol as needed for pain and stay well hydrated.
- If headache worsens, new symptoms (fever, rash) occur, or pattern changes, contact the clinic immediately.
- Arrange a blood pressure check and consider follow-up if headaches become recurrent or cycle-related.

Next Steps:
- Obtain and use a home thermometer; monitor for fever.
- Schedule a blood pressure check soon.
- Follow up with the clinic if no improvement, if headaches recur, or if triggers/patterns are identified.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing elements: No vitals (BP, temperature), no in-person neurologic exam, no fundoscopic exam, no neck stiffness assessment documented, medication doses/routes/frequencies not documented, pregnancy status not assessed.
- Internal conflicts: None significant; note that “aspirin allergy” manifests as nausea (may represent intolerance vs. true allergy).
- Transcript quality: Minor pauses/inaudible segments; adequate for clinical documentation.
